en: Where to Stay: Choose the District First
zh: 住在哪里：按街区选酒店
ja: どこに泊まるか：街区でホテルを選ぶ

p.src: Reaching South Gate and leaving the car does not always mean reaching the hotel. The booking pin may sit on one corner while the entrance opens on another side of the building. Yongning Gate and the wall across the road confirm the district, but the last few metres still need attention. The four guides keep their luggage beside the doorway, match the building and entrance to the reservation, then enter the lobby. Choose a Xi'an hotel in the same order: decide where the first morning should begin before comparing stars, views or breakfast.

caption.zh: 南门附近，四位向导把行李留在门侧，先核对建筑与实际入口，再进酒店。永宁门能确认住在城市哪一边，却不能替代最后一个街口和房间朝向的核验。
caption.ja: 南門近くで、四人は荷物を玄関脇にまとめ、建物と実際の入口を照合してからホテルへ入る。永寧門は市内のどちら側に泊まるかを示すが、最後の角や部屋の向きまでは教えない。
caption.en: Near South Gate, the four guides keep their luggage beside the doorway and match the building to the actual entrance before checking in. Yongning Gate confirms which side of the city they chose, but not the final corner or the room's direction.

p.src: Place the itinerary on the map and five anchors are enough. Inside the wall suits days built around Bell and Drum Tower, the Great Mosque, Beilin and the old lanes. South Gate joins the wall to the Line 2 north-south corridor. Yanta/Qujiang suits mornings around the Big Wild Goose Pagoda and museums, followed by an evening in the southern districts. The Xi'an North corridor matters only when an early or late high-speed train controls the plan. Lintong needs a reason to spend two consecutive days east of the city. These points mark lodging options; they are neither hotel boundaries nor live navigation.

caption.zh: 五个住处落点服务五种行程：城墙内、南门、雁塔／曲江、西安北站片区与临潼。数字表示选择顺序，不是酒店边界、完整地铁图、车程或实时导航。
caption.ja: 五つの宿泊拠点は、城壁内、南門、雁塔・曲江、西安北駅周辺、臨潼という五つの旅程に対応する。番号は選択の手掛かりであり、宿泊地区の境界、地下鉄全図、所要時間、当日のナビではない。
caption.en: Five stay anchors serve five itinerary shapes: inside the wall, South Gate, Yanta/Qujiang, the Xi'an North corridor and Lintong. The numbers frame a choice; they are not hotel boundaries, the complete metro, journey times or live navigation.

p.src: Inside the wall works well when the first morning begins by taking bearings at Bell Tower, continues through the lanes beyond Drum Tower, and adds Beilin or Shuyuanmen. Here, “central” means the compact old core within the Ming wall, not the centre of every attraction in modern Xi'an. Enlarge the booking map to the final corner: can a car reach the door, does the entrance face the main street or a lane, do restaurants or bars downstairs stay active late, and does the room face the street or an inner court? Hilton Garden Inn Xi'an Bell Tower at 15 Fenxiang Road is a current verification example. It shows why the street address matters; the words “Bell Tower” in a hotel name do not guarantee a location beside it.

p.src: South Gate is a useful compromise when you want access to both the old core and the southern city. Start early by seeing the scale of Yongning Gate and the wall, walk north into the old city, or use Line 2 south toward Small Wild Goose Pagoda and Xiaozhai. The gate remains a clear landmark when you return at night. The tradeoff is that traffic and street activity along Huancheng South Road can affect rooms differently. The official page for Hampton by Hilton Xi'an South Gate City Wall gives the specific address Building C, 18 West Section, Huancheng South Road, and describes Yongningmen and the metro as a short walk. The useful questions are more exact: which station exit reaches which entrance, and which way does the booked room face?

p.src: Base two days around the Big Wild Goose Pagoda, Shaanxi History Museum, Qujiang and southern evenings, and a daily commute from inside the wall makes little sense. Staying in Yanta/Qujiang reserves morning energy for timed entry and walking without cutting the evening short. In return, allow separately for Bell and Drum Tower, an early Xi'an North train or a full Lintong day. The Westin Xi'an's official page places it at 66 Ci'en Road, opposite the pagoda, and lists non-smoking, laundry, lift and accessibility details. A photograph does not guarantee a pagoda view; the booked category must state it.

p.src: Give the Xi'an North corridor priority only when an early or late high-speed train would otherwise cut into sleep, checkout or the time needed to enter the station. Search results may define “near Xi'an North” by straight-line distance or a broad business area; that does not mean a suitcase walk to the concourse. voco Xi'an ETDZ is at 39 Fengcheng 9th Road. Its official material describes Xi'an North as roughly 3 km away in a straight line and states that no local shuttle is available. That makes it a useful test: locate the actual station and hotel entrances on the map, then check metro or car access for the arrival hour. Never convert “near” into “walkable.” Without an early or late train, also count the daily journeys to and from the old city and Yanta.

p.src: Lintong is not a casual choice to be “a little closer to the Terracotta Army”; it is a complete itinerary. An overnight stay can work when the first day gives the archaeological site at the Qin museum enough time and the second adds Huaqing Palace, Mount Li or a deliberate hot-spring rest. The second morning then begins in the east rather than with another transfer from central Xi'an. For a single Terracotta Army visit, keeping the same room in Xi'an is usually easier. The current Angsana Xi'an Lintong page gives No. 8 East Yuechun Road and describes the property as about 200 m from Exit D of Zhiyang Guangchang on Line 9. Recheck that access before departure, and do not treat hotel-reported drive times as guarantees. Packing, checkout, luggage storage, transfer and a second check-in must all be counted as moving time.

p.src: Check ten items before paying. 1. The hotel's full Chinese name. 2. The branch, building and actual entrance. 3. The final transport available at the arrival hour. 4. King or twin beds and permitted occupancy. 5. Whether the room truly has an exterior window. 6. Non-smoking status written into the reservation. 7. Bathroom door, wet/dry separation and privacy. 8. Lift, step-free entrance or required assistance. 9. Breakfast, laundry, deposit and accepted payment. 10. Cancellation, change and late-arrival hold terms. For a foreign guest staying in a hotel, the hotel handles accommodation registration; keep a valid passport ready. Current national policy also says lodging operators and platforms should not use a supposed “foreign-guest qualification” as a barrier. If a platform remains vague, confirm directly before payment instead of leaving the uncertainty until check-in.

p.src: For two people, the costliest amenity is not always the most useful. Agree first on noise, darkness, and king or twin beds. Then check bathroom privacy, space for two open suitcases, sockets on both sides of the bed, somewhere to dry clothes, and whether the early riser can get ready quietly. Even if one traveler books, both should read the room type and cancellation terms. If the room differs, request a change using the written reservation, not a promotional photograph. A good room lets both travelers leave on schedule the next morning.

p.src: Most two- to five-day Xi'an trips need one city base. Changing hotels means packing, checking out, handling luggage, crossing the city, finding a second entrance and checking in again. Removing one afternoon ride does not automatically make the day easier. Split the stay for only two clear reasons: the final night near Xi'an North makes a very early high-speed train realistically reachable, or two consecutive days in Lintong end without returning to the old city on the second day. Even then, first ask whether the original hotel can store luggage, extend checkout or arrange a car; moving may be unnecessary. For a day trip to the Terracotta Army or Huashan, keep the same room and leave the luggage there.

p.src: Check six things. 1. Where the first day begins. 2. Which airport or station you need after the final night. 3. The hotel's full Chinese name, branch, building and entrance. 4. The last leg at the arrival hour. 5. Bed, window, non-smoking status, bathroom and occupancy in the booking. 6. Cancellation, late-arrival hold, deposit, payment and registration. Save the Chinese address, phone, entrance image and booking number offline; check them before payment and departure. Choose a room that lets the first day start on time and the last day end without a rush, not simply one that looks central.
